_about: What Knos can do and how far each thing has got. `stage` is the highest of `stages` that has evidence; scripts/capabilities.py checks the evidence (offline, and against devnet with --rpc) and renders the table in README.md. An exercised signature that no document of this repository gives is left out and filled by the release; nothing is `reproduced` until a document links someone else's run. Only a public program id is evidence for `deployed` and `exercised`: the `knos_*` addresses of programs-v2/program_ids.json and upgrade_gate's own `declare_id!`, each listed under `programs` with the version devnet runs there (`on_chain`). A deployment of a build at an address of its own (the 0.3.14 rehearsal's staging programs) is never evidence: what ran there is said in the capability's note, with its transaction, and the capability stays `tested` until a transaction at a public id exercises it. docs/CAPABILITIES.md lists the rehearsal's transactions.

capabilities.what: A neutral run that finds the paid head failing, sent inside the order's warranty, returns the holdback to the funder.
capabilities.note: Rehearsed on a staging deployment of the knos_pay 2.1 build (signature 5H6mrHjgLhRxgFNWLa8p1R5BVhgzsU22Yj2b6AGbqzANCiaHLKRN6XuVYziRaTiQaqTL4pFwpfTnnRMS3csi3EL5; docs/CAPABILITIES.md, "The 0.3.14 rehearsal on devnet"), not on the public program ids: the public knos_pay and knos_oidc carry it only once their upgrade to 2.1 has executed, and no transaction there is recorded yet. The neutral run came from another repository than the order's, inside the warranty; it signed because the paid pull request's merge had been reverted, not by running the checks on the head again. Only what the order still holds returns: what was paid at acceptance stays paid, and after the warranty no challenge is heard.

The knos_pay 2.2 build of this tree counts judges by repository owner and binds their markers to the order's funding (`quorum_by_owner`): tested, not deployed.

capabilities.what: A GitHub Action gives a verdict on a pull request from GitHub's record of the commit, with a read-only token, and it has never run on GitHub.
capabilities.note: Tested with a stand-in for GitHub's API. docs/RELEASE.md has the first real run as a step after the push.

capabilities.what: A platform can verify a bundle's evidence itself with one file, in Python or TypeScript, and both answer every case the same.
capabilities.note: No platform uses it (docs/INTEGRATIONS.md).

capabilities.what: `knos init` writes the hook each of ten agent hosts reads, into the project only, and none has been run inside a real host.
capabilities.note: Each route is tested against the event its host documents, recorded in tests/_host_events.py; no host application was started.

capabilities.what: The built verifier and an independent reference gave the same answer on 8,855 generated tokens, with 0 disagreements.
capabilities.note: The recorded run is docs/fuzz.json, against the test build of knos_oidc 2.2. No class of token is outside the rule: the 13 shapes of a signed payload that is not strict JSON in a value the verifier does not read, which 2.1 accepted, are refused.

capabilities.what: A fuzz target asks the program's RSA arithmetic, big integers and the `rsa` crate whether each input is an RS256 signature, and fails when they differ.
capabilities.note: A harness beside the program; the program's source is unchanged. Its seeds are the differential cases and the Wycheproof vectors; the nightly job fuzzes it for five minutes.

capabilities.what: `knos --version` and each single command start without importing the other commands' modules.
A tab keeps what it read, draws a view at once from what was kept, reads again, and says how old a view is when the second read fails.

tested.names: cache: what one page kept, the next page of the tab reads

capabilities.note: The test is a Node script that needs a browser; run it with `node tests/web/live.mjs`.

capabilities.what: The site shows the latest canary round stage by stage with GitHub's and devnet's own times, and never draws an old round as live.

tested.names: live, stale: a round three hours old is the last round

capabilities.note: Tested against a mocked GitHub and a mocked devnet with the clock held; run it with `node tests/web/live.mjs`.

capabilities.what: The mark and the wordmark are one drawing in every copy: the README's header, the site's icon, the card and the badge.
Shadow mode reads an invoice that bills per merged change and says which billed changes had a failed check when they were merged.
capabilities.note: Never run against live GitHub: every test reads a recording, and the page (web/shadow.js, tests/test_site_shadow.py) is driven with a mocked API. No buyer's invoice has been checked with it.

capabilities.what: A stranger funds a test order in the playground repository by opening one issue, inside limits on the amount, the slots and the day.
capabilities.note: Not live until its repository is published: the tests run the rules and draw the page from mocked data, and no stranger has funded anything there. The money is the devnet faucet's test USDC.

capabilities.what: The first screen replays one recorded round in six steps a visitor drives with the keyboard, and shows nothing the repository does not record.
capabilities.note: A replay of recorded data (web/demo_data.json), not a live round. Its replay step is recorded as error 83, the order is not in the state this needs (already paid), not as the single-use error.

capabilities.what: The site has one set of variables and classes for surface, depth and motion, a first screen of forty words at most, and no movement for a reader who asks for none.
capabilities.note: The browser part needs node, the playwright package and Chromium (tests/web/motion.mjs); without them it is skipped.

capabilities.what: Eleven issuers of RS256 workload tokens are documented with what the verifier takes from each, and a token of each one's shape verifies under a key registered for its address.
capabilities.note: Tested in the Solana runtime with keys made in the test: no issuer but GitHub and GitLab has signed a token Knos verified. The deployed verifier refuses ES256, ES384 and PS256 tokens; ES256 is a capability of its own (es256_tokens).

capabilities.what: An accepted deliverable is exported as one bill line in the import formats of several accounting products, each file with the statement's hash.
capabilities.note: The SAP and Coupa files are best effort and unverified: their columns come from the products' public notes, and no file has been imported into either product. Runs on the author's machine: there is no program to deploy.

capabilities.what: Version 2 of the audit file also lists an organisation's bounties, what is still owed, and the buyer's own references.
capabilities.note: A file of version 1 still verifies. Runs on the author's machine: there is no program to deploy.

capabilities.what: Every deliverable is shown as four linked records made from the statement alone: authorisation, acceptance, commercial record and settlement status.
capabilities.note: The site makes the same four from the same rows (web/finance_data.js, tests/web/finance.mjs). Settlement on devnet is a demonstration in test USDC.

capabilities.what: A payment goes through five named states (received, accepted, submitted, confirmed, finalized), the same in the workflow's comment, the relay log and the site.
Every line the relay logs for a payment carries when it was queued, seen, sent and confirmed, whoever relayed it.
capabilities.note: Lines written before this release carry no stage times; scripts/latency_stages.py lists those payments apart.

capabilities.what: A funding comment names a third reader, a repository neither side owns, and an order with a quorum of three pays only when all three passed the same artifact.
capabilities.note: Runs at the public id only once the upgrade to `knos_pay 2.1` has executed (the live state is in web/upgrades.json). Two readers of one owner count as one.

capabilities.what: An outcome that is not a merged pull request is funded by one comment from a template, and only the honest file is paid.
capabilities.note: The flow test is the data-labelling example of examples/outcomes, run in the Solana runtime; the other outcomes have a template and no flow test.

capabilities.what: Published terms are files named by their hash that are never rewritten, and a contract can cite one in a sentence both sides can check.
capabilities.note: No contract is known to cite these terms.

capabilities.what: Every settlement is remembered through Sibyl, and a funding comment is offered terms from that memory and nothing from an empty one.
capabilities.note: The memory is the repository's own Sibyl store; without Sibyl nothing is proposed.

capabilities.what: The weekly index sample stays inside a fixed budget of requests and minutes, publishes what it has, and resumes from its checkpoint.
capabilities.note: Tested against a recorded GitHub; the scheduled workflow has not yet published a week from this sample.

capabilities.what: The tamper benchmark also measures how much honest work each judge accepts, and lists every honest submission a judge refused with its reason.
capabilities.note: The black-box judge accepted 61 of 61 honest submissions, of which the 48 of the set before, 48 of 48; cheats accepted: 0 of 63, 0 of 102, 0 of 25 on tasks that are not code and 0 of 14 new ones, every figure from one run of the whole benchmark in this release (docs/TAMPER.md, docs/ASSURANCE.md). Knos's own tasks and submissions; nobody outside has run the set.

capabilities.what: Each program is followed from source commit to build hash to the hash on chain to its upgrade proposal, and a link the repository does not record is printed as MISSING.
capabilities.note: No program's chain is complete in the committed record (docs/PROVENANCE.md): the exercised scenario is MISSING for each, the execution transaction is MISSING while its proposal has not executed, and the knos_oidc and knos_pay builds that run at the public ids before the upgrade have no build record.

capabilities.what: A kit of vectors lets another implementation show, case by case, that it reads Knos's formats as Knos does.
capabilities.note: Run only against Knos's own Python and JavaScript; no outside implementation has run it.

capabilities.what: A release publishes a crate or a package at its own version, and only a version the registry lacks.
capabilities.note: Tested against a mocked registry index; the rule first runs for real in the release of 0.3.16.

capabilities.what: The verifier reads every value of a token's header and payload as strict JSON and refuses a token that is not.
capabilities.note: knos_oidc 2.2 is not deployed: it will be proposed after the pending upgrade executes, and until that proposal has executed devnet runs an earlier version, which accepts such a token (the live state is in web/upgrades.json).

capabilities.what: Every place where a program's source writes a panic is listed with the reason it cannot be reached or what happens when it is.
capabilities.note: The list is docs/UNWRAPS.md. Indexing is counted by file, not explained line by line.

capabilities.what: One outcome that is not code is signed by a Kubernetes cluster's service-account issuer, checked offline by the verifier's rule and verified under a private key.

asserted: knos_oidc verified a token of the issuer https://kind.knos-outcome.invalid, a Kubernetes cluster's own, under a private key this wallet registered
the token's account 9CYHPf7tbPmPyFN1CCCZDVaNCLDi7CcXZTcDx99aX8qV names that issuer's hash and the registrant 9ig9AXfoNrd5uPhdSFGujPoVsrxze5CGVFM6uusgQydG
the same token passed the verifier's rule offline first; the meter does not count it on chain

capabilities.note: Tested with a test key; a kind cluster's token was verified offline in staging run 37483745385 of drexthealpha/knos-rc (https://github.com/drexthealpha/knos-rc/actions/runs/37483745385); nothing of it is on devnet, and the meter does not count it on chain.

capabilities.what: One append-only log of events sits under every recording mode, with durable ids, signed acknowledgements, corrections and duplicate detection.
capabilities.note: A file beside the ledgers, written when a recording command is given --events or KNOS_EVENTS; nothing on chain reads it.

capabilities.what: One invoice becomes a statement as JSON, CSV and PDF that say the same; each line is agreed, disputed, duplicate or has insufficient evidence, and anyone rebuilds it from its evidence.
capabilities.note: Made from example evidence; no buyer's invoice has been run through it.

capabilities.what: A receipt of version 4 says one of four verdicts, only an accepted one authorises payment, and a deliverable, an evaluation, an invoice line and a settlement each have an id of their own.
capabilities.note: The programs on chain know accepted and rejected only; the other two verdicts are recorded off chain.

capabilities.what: The relay takes tokens through a queue with leases: several workers, each payer's tokens in order, a killed worker's entry taken again, nothing sent twice.
capabilities.note: Tested against a simulated relay and clock; the public relay's sweep has not run on it on devnet.

capabilities.what: An evidence bundle is sealed to the buyer, the supplier and an auditor, exported, kept under a retention policy and restored from the export alone after the working copy and the chain are gone.
capabilities.note: The restore drill runs on files made in the test; no outside party holds a key.

capabilities.what: A private repository's verdict leaves as a record of a verdict word and hashes, signed for by an attestor both parties approved; the code stays where it is.
capabilities.note: Nobody has run it in a private repository.

capabilities.what: A supplier checks a change against an order's terms before submitting it, and is told which line of the terms a refusal would cite and what was refused before under the same terms.
A supplier contests a rejection: the verdict moves to disputed with who, when and why, and the neutral judge's re-run overturns or upholds it in plain words.
capabilities.note: The `/knos appeal` comment is read by the workflow's job; no appeal has been opened outside the tests.

capabilities.what: Every refusal the programs, the terms, the judge and the comment parser can give has a row of two plain sentences: what happened and what to do.
A month's invoice is Control, Meter, Acceptance on value reconciled off chain and record lookups; value released on chain is never charged again, and every line names the rule that produced it.
capabilities.note: Arithmetic on example months. Nobody has been invoiced: nothing has been sold and there is no legal entity to invoice from.

capabilities.what: The Agent PR Index is a weekly leaderboard with a 95% interval and the sample size on every row, a minimum sample to be placed, and a dispute path whose open and resolved cases are published.
capabilities.note: No dispute has been filed.

capabilities.what: The site's first control checks a pasted supplier invoice or a named public repository in place: a neutral count and every mismatch, with no install, wallet or sign-up.
capabilities.note: The browser part needs node, the playwright package and Chromium (tests/web/front_door.mjs); without them it is skipped.

capabilities.what: An ES256 token is verified in one transaction: Solana's secp256r1 precompile checks the signature, and `VerifyEs256` checks that what it verified is the issuer's key, the token and its signature.
capabilities.note: A Rust test crate (`cd programs-v2/handlers && cargo test`), run by the program workflow and not by pytest. In the default build of knos_oidc in this tree (202,032 bytes; the verifier's data account on devnet has room for 279,360, so no extension is needed) and NOT deployed: no public program id runs it, and the build is not proposed yet. Two fixed test keys; no token of a real ES256 issuer has been verified. A signing input of at most 780 bytes (docs/ES256.md).

capabilities.what: A correct fix that adds its own regression test is accepted: an added test file runs and is not counted, an existing protected test edited or deleted is refused, and the funder's suite alone decides.
capabilities.note: Measured on Knos's own tasks (docs/TAMPER.md): 61 of 61 honest submissions accepted, 0 of 14 cheats aimed at what a pull request may now add. `knos preflight` and the supplier page give the same answer from the same rule.

capabilities.what: Standing offers, rate cards and budget envelopes are read from files and held to each other; an envelope shows before and after and refuses by the amount over.
capabilities.note: Files in a repository, checked by the command line. The funding workflow does not ask the gate yet, and nothing on chain reads them.

capabilities.what: An approval counts only from an account that holds the role on that day and within its limit; a self-approval above the limit is refused, and the chain says what waits for whom.
capabilities.note: `knos approve record | check | status`. An approval's author and time are the forge's; the funding workflow does not ask the gate yet.

capabilities.what: Kani proves on the program's own lines that an order's fee is at least 0.05, is 0.05 or at most 0.30% of the amount, and adds to the amount in a u64.
capabilities.note: For amounts from 0 to 100,000.00 at 6 decimals and rates from 10 to 30 basis points, one rate and no tiers (the knos_pay 2.2 build of this tree, not deployed). docs/kani.json `fee_proofs`, status `verified but for one bound at one rate`; its `parts` say which statement is verified over which amounts and rates. The test holds the record to the source's hash: no test of this repository runs Kani itself.

capabilities.what: What an opponent would try is replayed against the built programs: an address funded again, the second before and after every time limit, a payment and a refund together, one token twice, one judge under a quorum.
capabilities.note: A Rust test crate (`cd programs-v2/handlers && cargo test --release --test adversarial`), not run by pytest. Two of its tests are ignored because the program as built fails them: one account can be two judges of a wallet's order, and a judge's marker outlives its order by a second (docs/SECURITY.md). Neither is fixed in this release.

capabilities.what: A program of its own, built against the published interface crate only, releases once for its own workflow's token and refuses five mistakes a reader can make.
capabilities.note: An example in a workspace of its own, not deployed. No program outside this repository is known to read the verifier.

capabilities.what: A page makes a member key in the browser, keeps the private half with the person and asks with the public half only; one command adds the holder.
capabilities.note: Outside key holders: 0. One person, the founder, holds every member key of both multisigs (docs/KEYHOLDER.md, docs/GOVERNANCE.md); nobody has asked.

capabilities.what: An order's and a job's fee is one rate: 0.30% of the amount, floor 0.05, no maximum and no tiers; a Plan lowers it to no less than 0.10%.
capabilities.note: In the knos_pay 2.2 build of this tree: tested in the simulator, not deployed. The build is proposed after the release and is not live at the public id until that proposal executes (web/upgrades.json). Until then the public program charges the 0.3.14 fee (`fee_tiers`); orders funded before the upgrade keep the rate fixed at their funding.

capabilities.what: A quorum counts judges by repository owner, the neutral judge differs from both sides in owner and actor, and a judge's marker counts only for the funding of the order it was made under.
capabilities.note: In the knos_pay 2.2 build of this tree: tested in the simulator, not deployed. The build is proposed after the release and is not live at the public id until that proposal executes (web/upgrades.json). What the program cannot know: that two accounts are two people.

capabilities.what: An order may give a token issued by its deadline a grace in which it can still be presented; the refund follows when no such token can live.
capabilities.note: In the knos_pay 2.2 build of this tree: tested in the simulator, not deployed. The build is proposed after the release and is not live at the public id until that proposal executes (web/upgrades.json).

capabilities.what: A batch's commitment (format 2) hashes each complete canonical event, so swapping which of two equal-priced evaluations was accepted changes the root.
capabilities.note: Tested on ledger files; no format 2 batch is anchored on the public ids. knos_meter is unchanged: the root is opaque to the program.

capabilities.what: A supplier's public record is one file: each deliverable counted once, with the evidence behind every count.
capabilities.note: The committed records are cut from the public index of agent pull requests; no supplier outside Knos has a record of paid work.

capabilities.what: A badge is drawn from a supplier's record, states its sample and is green only for accepted work.
capabilities.note: Nobody outside Knos shows one.

capabilities.what: A verified receipt becomes one page to attach to an invoice, with the file that proves it.
capabilities.note: No invoice has been sent with one.

capabilities.what: One line in a supplier's repository runs the free check on every pull request, posts once and attaches the receipt.
capabilities.note: A reusable workflow called at a release's tag; it has not run in a repository outside Knos.

capabilities.what: Knos Terms 3 is a versioned document that answers ten questions; a file missing one is refused by name, and two versions diff by meaning.
capabilities.note: `knos terms verify` and `knos terms diff` read it. Funding does not enforce a terms 3 document yet.

capabilities.what: Terms 3 are proposed from a repository's own record: the checks that passed on every recent merge, its test directories and its code owners.
capabilities.note: Tested on recorded answers of GitHub's API. A repository with no merge in 30 days gets no proposal.

capabilities.what: A decision is given the moment the evidence arrives, as a provisional receipt that never authorises payment; the final receipt names the one it supersedes.
capabilities.note: `knos decide`. The workflows and the relay do not post it yet.

capabilities.what: Relay runs keep notes that merge by key, so two runners carry one token once; each lane pays from its own fee payer.
capabilities.note: Tested with stand-in runners and a stand-in chain; the public relay runs with one fee payer.

capabilities.what: A verdict crosses from the job that runs a pull request's code to the job that signs as one line of fixed fields, read as data and checked again from GitHub's record.
capabilities.note: The signing job runs none of the pull request's code. Tested on recorded answers; the published workflows carry it from the next republish.

capabilities.what: An agent pays another agent only when an evaluator signs the acceptance; wrong work releases nothing and the buyer is refunded at expiry.
capabilities.note: Separate processes against the test builds of knos_pay and knos_oidc in the simulator, in test USDC; no outside agent has used it.

capabilities.what: Nothing is sent to, opened on or recommended for an outside repository unless it merged a pull request in the last 30 days; what cannot be read is a refusal.
capabilities.note: Tested on recorded answers of GitHub's API; the date of the last merge is printed.

capabilities.what: A claim on an issue or log that holds no funded order gets one automatic answer and a label, once.
capabilities.note: Runs from .github/workflows/claims.yml on this repository; tested on recorded events.
